findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~186 (`SpanFlusher.main`): `for flushed_segment in flushed_segment.values():` iterates the loop variable this very statement introduces instead of `flushed_segments.values()`, raising NameError the first time there is anything to flush, crash-looping the flusher (restart → MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS → consumer restart) so no spans are ever produced.

[High/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~245 (`_ensure_processes_alive`): `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for processes created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` (SpawnProcess subclasses BaseProcess, not context.Process), so `process.kill()` is never executed; a hung flusher is no longer killed before its replacement starts (regression — old code called kill() unconditionally), leaving two workers polling the same shards → duplicate segment production/duplicate spans in Kafka plus a leaked process per restart. The same broken check in `join()` means `terminate()` is never called either. Use `self.produce_to_pipe is None` or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess)`.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~49 + src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:~431: `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is unvalidated — a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max, len(shards))` negative so `range(num_processes)` is empty and zero flusher processes are created, causing the consumer to silently never flush while continuing to write to Redis (unbounded growth, no error); `0` silently becomes one process per shard due to `max_processes or len(...)`. Validate ≥ 1 (e.g., `click.IntRange(min=1)`).

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:~61: the added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`; the 'Give flusher threads time to process' comment is false and the drift→flush handoff remains unsynchronized (a flusher thread may observe `stopped` before acting on the new drift), leaving the test racy. Use a real synchronization primitive (event/condition) instead.

[Medium/test_gap] flusher.py: the PR's headline health-monitoring/restart logic (`_ensure_processes_alive`: hang/crash detection, per-process restart counting, kill-and-replace, `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`) has no test coverage; `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts internal mapping counts. A restart test would have caught the NameError and broken isinstance issues.

[Medium/data] flusher.py:~186–199 (`main`): `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of every shard in the process used as a single tag value on hot-path metrics (`flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, `wait_produce`); with the default `--flusher-processes 1` the tag embeds the entire shard list, commas inside a tag value corrupt statsd tag parsing (tags are comma-separated key:value pairs), and it's inconsistent with `flusher_unhealthy` which tags individual shard ids.

[Low/data] flusher.py:~186 vs ~196: tag key inconsistency — `flusher.produce`/`segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}` while `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}` for the same dimension, splitting dashboards/queries.

[Low/bug] flusher.py:~335 (`join`): when the deadline expires, `break` exits the for-loop, skipping `terminate()` for all remaining processes; on timeout, every process after the current one is left un-terminated.

[Low/api] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:41 and flusher.py:47: new `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` parameters are inserted before `produce_to_pipe`, shifting positional-argument positions; any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally now silently binds it to the new parameter (for the factory, `produce_to_pipe` would silently stay `None`). Append new keyword params at the end of the signature.

[Low/doc_defect] flusher.py:~30: docstring 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' is inaccurate — the process count is `min(max_processes, len(shards))` and the CLI default (`--flusher-processes 1`) is a single process handling all shards.
[Low/bug] flusher.py:~125: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code (never called anywhere in the diff); it would also spawn a replacement without killing the old process if ever used. Remove it.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~49 + src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:~431: `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is unvalidated — a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max, len(shards))` negative so `range(num_processes)` is empty and zero flusher processes are created, causing the consumer to silently never flush while continuing to write to Redis (unbounded growth, no error); `0` silently becomes one process per shard due to `max_processes or len(...)`. Validate ≥ 1 (e.g., `click.IntRange(min=1)`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no range validation, and threads it through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(flusher_processes)` to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as “unset” (falls back to `len(...)`), and a negative value is truthy so it is accepted. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative; `process_to_shards_map` becomes empty (`range(negative)`), and the subsequent shard distribution loop will attempt `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)` on missing keys (likely raising `KeyError`) or otherwise leaving no processes created. This is a real misconfiguration-driven failure mode introduced by the change and should be prevented via validation (e.g., Click range min=1) or explicit checks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new health/restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` (per-process hang/crash detection via `process.is_alive()` and `process_healthy_since[...]`, per-process restart counting in `self.process_restarts[...]`, kill-and-recreate via `_create_process_for_shards`, and raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). The newly added test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts `processes` count and shard mapping totals; it does not exercise the new unhealthy-path behavior (hang detection, crash detection, kill/restart, restart-limit error). Existing test changes similarly don’t cover restart behavior. So the finding about a meaningful test gap for this newly introduced nontrivial logic is grounded in the diff. The mention of specific bugs like a NameError is not verifiable from the diff, but the core test-coverage concern remains valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] flusher.py:~186–199 (`main`): `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of every shard in the process used as a single tag value on hot-path metrics (`flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, `wait_produce`); with the default `--flusher-processes 1` the tag embeds the entire shard list, commas inside a tag value corrupt statsd tag parsing (tags are comma-separated key:value pairs), and it's inconsistent with `flusher_unhealthy` which tags individual shard ids.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the diff introduces `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and then uses it as a single metric tag value on hot-path metrics (`metrics.timer(... tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing(... tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timer(... tags={"shards": shard_tag})`). This is diff-grounded and creates a potentially high-cardinality/awkward tag value (and even inconsistent key name `shard` vs `shards`), while other metrics like `flusher_unhealthy` tag individual shard ids (`tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`). However, the claim that commas in the tag value definitively “corrupt statsd tag parsing” cannot be verified from the diff alone (depends on the metrics backend/encoder), so it’s better treated as a metrics design/consistency concern rather than a provable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:41 and flusher.py:47: new `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` parameters are inserted before `produce_to_pipe`, shifting positional-argument positions; any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally now silently binds it to the new parameter (for the factory, `produce_to_pipe` would silently stay `None`). Append new keyword params at the end of the signature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show both `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` and `SpanFlusher.__init__` gaining a new optional parameter (`flusher_processes` / `max_processes`) inserted *before* the existing `produce_to_pipe` parameter, changing the positional-argument order (factory.py: `flusher_processes: int | None = None, produce_to_pipe=...`; flusher.py: `max_processes: int | None = None, produce_to_pipe=...`). That creates a real API-compatibility footgun: any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally would now bind it to the new parameter. However, from this diff alone we cannot verify that any call sites actually pass `produce_to_pipe` positionally (the updated/added tests use keyword args, and the internal construction uses keywords), so it’s not a confirmed broken behavior in the shown changes, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] flusher.py:~30: docstring 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' is inaccurate — the process count is `min(max_processes, len(shards))` and the CLI default (`--flusher-processes 1`) is a single process handling all shards.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`’s docstring it says “Creates one process per shard for parallel processing,” but the implementation sets `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and then assigns multiple shards to a process via modulo mapping (`process_index = i % self.num_processes`). Additionally, the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to `1` (in `consumers/__init__.py`), which would commonly result in a single process handling all shards. This is a real, diff-grounded documentation inaccuracy, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py:~125: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code (never called anywhere in the diff); it would also spawn a replacement without killing the old process if ever used. Remove it.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `_create_process_for_shard` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the shown diff (the code paths use `_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive`). So the “dead code” part is verifiable. Also, as written it calls `_create_process_for_shards` without killing/terminating any existing process for that `process_index`, which would risk leaving an old process running and overwriting `self.processes[process_index]` if it were ever used. This is a concrete maintainability/latent-correctness issue, but not an observed functional bug since it’s unused in the diff.
